figurative_meaning_en: A woman with the demeanor and mannerisms of a European lady
example_sentences_in_english: She walks and behaves like a memsahib.
history: Originated during the British colonial period in India and Bengal, where 'memsahib' referred to European women, often wives of British officials; in Bengali usage, it describes local women imitating Western styles of dress and behavior.
note: This term carries a colonial connotation and may imply a sense of Western imitation in post-colonial contexts.
